title: Presidential Candidates' Agendas on Friday (2) Ahead of the First Round
subtitle: Candidates held walkabouts, rallies, and other campaign events in various cities
excerpt: On Friday (2), presidential candidates' schedules featured walkabouts, rallies, and campaign events in various locations, just before the first round of elections.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In the final days leading up to the first round of the 2026 elections, Friday (2) was marked by intense activity from presidential candidates. In several cities across the country, the presidential hopefuls' schedules included walkabouts, rallies, and other campaign events, showcasing the candidates' mobilization in the final stages of the race.

Campaign Events in Various Locations

Candidates took advantage of the day to traverse streets, participate in public events, and hold rallies, aiming for direct contact with voters. These actions are part of the outreach strategy outlined in the electoral calendar, which permits campaign events until the eve of voting.

Electoral Calendar Context

The period preceding the first round of elections is characterized by an intense schedule, during which candidates escalate their visits to municipalities, organize public demonstrations, and reinforce their messages across media platforms. This dynamic is stipulated in the rules governing the electoral process, ensuring that competitors have the opportunity to present their proposals before polling closes.

With information from Agência Brasil.
